questions.q: What character starts a Data Factory expression?
questions.explain: Every dynamic expression starts with @. A literal @ character is written as @@ to escape it.

questions.q: What's the practical difference between @pipeline().parameters.myNumber and @{pipeline().parameters.myNumber}?
options: The bare expression preserves the original type (e.g. a number); the @{...} form forces a string result
They are functionally identical in every case
The @{...} form only works inside a ForEach activity
The bare expression only works with string parameters
questions.explain: A bare @expression returns its native type. Wrapping it in @{...} — string interpolation — forces the result into a string, useful for building dynamic file names or messages.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the six built-in function categories?
questions.explain: The six categories are Date/Time, String, Collection, Logical, Conversion, and Math. Visualization isn't a Data Factory expression function category — that's a Power BI concern.

options: This specific pipeline run's unique ID
The name of the data factory
The name of whichever activity is currently running
questions.explain: RunId is a pipeline-scope system variable identifying this particular run — useful for logging or building unique file names per run.

questions.q: For a Schedule trigger, what's the difference between @trigger().scheduledTime and @trigger().startTime?
options: scheduledTime is when it was supposed to fire; startTime is when it actually did (they can differ slightly)
They are always identical, down to the millisecond
scheduledTime only exists for Storage event triggers
startTime is only available inside a ForEach activity
questions.explain: scheduledTime is the planned trigger time; startTime is when the trigger actually fired to invoke the pipeline run, which can differ slightly from the schedule.
